world-scholars-cup-tbilisi-round-2027.about:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students that rewards curiosity rather than memorisation. Teams of three study an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music, literature and social studies, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz). Rounds also include community events such as the Scholar's Show (talent show).

This is a regional round in Tbilisi, Georgia, on 13–14 March 2027, hosted by British International School of Tbilisi. Students can join through a school club or as an independent team of three from any country; results can qualify teams for a Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.
highlights: Four team events: debate, collaborative writing, quiz bowl and challenge test
Open to independent teams as well as school clubs
Qualifies strong teams for a Global Round and the Yale Tournament of Champions
world-scholars-cup-tbilisi-round-2027.eligibility: School students (typically ages 10–18) in teams of three, from any school or country; independent teams are welcome. Divisions: Senior (born on or before 1 July 2013) and Junior (younger); scholars must be born on or before 31 December 2016.
how_to_apply: Form a team of three (school club or independent)
Open the WSC registration portal and choose this round (or use the round's Request Info link)
Register the team and any accompanying adults, and pay the fee by card or bank transfer
Study the 2026–27 theme and curriculum before the round
Attend the round in Tbilisi, 13–14 March 2027
world-scholars-cup-tbilisi-round-2027.costs: Registration fee per scholar (student): regular 60 USD, late 75 USD. Adults/coaches register separately; travel, accommodation and most meals are extra. Payment by card or bank transfer through the WSC portal.

ihbb-dubai-2027.about:
The International History Bee and Bowl (IHBB), run by International Academic Competitions, is a buzzer-based history quiz for school students. The History Bowl is a team event (up to a full school team, with 2-person and solo options) and the History Bee is an individual event; questions cover world history, geography and culture. The 2027 History Bee and Bowl of Dubai takes place at Dubai College, Dubai, on 24 January 2027.

Students compete in age divisions (Varsity, Junior Varsity, Middle School and Elementary, by date of birth). Students can also sit the Science Bee and Geography Bee qualifying exams during the lunch break. Top students and teams qualify for the 2027 IHBB European Championships and world-level IAC events such as the International History Olympiad. It is a good first international competition for students who love history and quizzes.
highlights: Team (Bowl) and individual (Bee) history quiz in one day
Science Bee and Geography Bee qualifying exams available on site
Qualifies students for the 2027 European Championships and world events
ihbb-dubai-2027.eligibility: School students from any school, entered by their school (or a coach) in age-based divisions: Varsity, Junior Varsity, Middle School and Elementary. Teams can be full, 2-person or solo.
how_to_apply: Check the tournament on the IHBB Europe upcoming-events page
Have your school or coach fill in the regional tournament registration form
Register before 16 January 2027 and pay by card or bank transfer
Practise with past IHBB question sets
Attend the tournament in Dubai on 24 January 2027
ihbb-dubai-2027.costs: 2026–27 in-person fees: History Bowl full team GBP 270 / EUR 310 / CHF 315 / USD 335 for fee-charging schools (GBP 145 / EUR 170 / CHF 210 / USD 200 for tuition-free schools); 2-person teams pay 2/3 and solo players 1/3 of the team price; History Bee included with the Bowl; extra exams GBP/EUR/CHF 20 or USD 25. Travel extra.

boulder-school-machine-learning-condense.about:
The Boulder School for Condensed Matter and Materials Physics at the University of Colorado Boulder is a long-running NSF-funded summer school with a new theme each year. The 2027 school (5–30 July 2027), coordinated by Roger Melko (Waterloo/Perimeter), Ehsan Khatami (San José State), Juan Carrasquilla (ETH) and Leo Radzihovsky (CU Boulder), introduces graduate students to the exchange between machine learning and many-body physics: foundations of ML theory and methods, statistical mechanics of learning, data-driven learning in classical and quantum systems, neural quantum states and applications to superconductivity, magnetism, atomic systems and quantum simulators.

Lecturers include researchers from Waterloo, Google, Leipzig, Los Alamos, UCSD, Perimeter, Flatiron/UBC and Munich. Students are expected to stay for the full four weeks. Accepted students pay a USD 400 registration fee; dormitory rooms are provided free (double occupancy by default) with weekday meals, and US-based students can get travel support, but students at universities outside the US must pay their own airfare.
highlights: Four weeks of lectures by top researchers in ML and quantum many-body physics
Free dorm housing in Boulder; modest USD 400 fee
Strong networking for future PhD/postdoc work
boulder-school-machine-learning-condense.eligibility: Primarily graduate students (and some postdocs) in condensed-matter, materials, quantum or computational physics and related fields, from any country. Students from universities outside the US are welcome but must fund their own airfare. Full attendance is expected.
how_to_apply: Complete the electronic application on the Boulder School site by 15 January 2027
Name a recommender, who is emailed automatically to upload a letter
If accepted, pay the USD 400 registration fee and arrange a US visa
Plan to attend the whole school (5–30 July 2027)
boulder-school-machine-learning-condense.costs: Registration fee USD 400. Dormitory rooms free (double occupancy by default); meals except weekends covered. Travel support up to USD 500 only for students at US universities; international students pay their own airfare.

bristol-quantum-in-the-summer-2027.about:
Quantum in the Summer is the annual summer school of the University of Bristol's Quantum Engineering Technology Labs, one of Europe's leading quantum photonics groups. Over one intensive week on the Bristol campus, students start from classical optics through a mix of lab work and lectures and move on to classical and quantum computing, quantum algorithms and quantum key distribution. Instructors (Bristol quantum researchers) also share their experience of a scientific career, and there are evening socials.

The 2027 school runs 2–6 August 2027 for students aged 16 and over (16–18 by the start) who are studying maths and physics at A-level or equivalent and have completed the first year of that study. It is open to UK students and to international students who can obtain a UK visa. The school itself is free (lunches provided), but participants cover their own accommodation, travel and dinners unless they receive one of a limited number of bursaries, which cover accommodation, travel and food. Applications open in March 2027 and include a CV; applicants from groups under-represented in STEM are particularly welcome.
highlights: Hands-on optics and quantum technology labs at a top UK quantum group
Free; bursaries cover accommodation, travel and food
Open to international students (with UK visa)
bristol-quantum-in-the-summer-2027.eligibility: Students aged 16–18 at the start of the school who have completed their GCSEs (or equivalent) and the first year of A-levels (or equivalent), are studying maths and physics, have strong mathematical ability and can attend the full week. Open to students from anywhere in the UK and to international students who can obtain a UK visa (e.g. a Georgian or Qatari student in the equivalent of grade 11–12).
how_to_apply: Watch the Quantum in the Summer page; applications open in March 2027
Prepare a CV (a template is provided on the page)
Submit the application and say if you want to be considered for a bursary
International applicants: check UK visa requirements early (processing takes weeks)
bristol-quantum-in-the-summer-2027.costs: Free tuition and lunches. Participants pay accommodation, travel and dinners unless awarded one of the limited bursary places, which cover accommodation, travel and food.

cambridge-ellis-summer-school-probabilis.about:
The ELLIS Cambridge Unit (part of the European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems) has organised a summer school every year since 2022. Its Summer School on Probabilistic Machine Learning brings together graduate students, researchers and professionals for a week of lectures by well-known researchers and industry scientists on advanced machine-learning topics such as probabilistic modelling, Bayesian deep learning, generative models and machine learning for the sciences. The 2026 edition (13–17 July) was held at the University of Cambridge's Department of Engineering and at Pembroke College.

Admission is selective via an online application (deadline 17 May in 2026, decisions by 31 May). There is no tuition fee, and lunch and refreshments are provided; attendees cover their own travel and accommodation, and participants who fly to Cambridge pay a GBP 500 'sustainability' fee that is waived for those arriving by train or bus. Travel grants are offered after selection to participants from under-represented backgrounds.
highlights: Week of lectures by leading probabilistic-ML researchers in Cambridge
Networking within the European ELLIS AI community
Travel grants for under-represented participants
cambridge-ellis-summer-school-probabilis.eligibility: Graduate students (master's/PhD), researchers and professionals working in or moving into machine learning; strong undergraduates with ML background may also apply. Open to all nationalities (UK visa rules apply).
how_to_apply: Check the ELLIS Cambridge summer-school page for the 2027 edition (expected spring 2027)
Submit the online application before the deadline (17 May in 2026)
Decisions about two weeks later; selected participants can then apply for a travel grant
Book accommodation (options listed under Practical Information)
cambridge-ellis-summer-school-probabilis.costs: No tuition; lunch and refreshments provided. Participants pay travel and accommodation; those flying to Cambridge pay a GBP 500 sustainability fee (waived for land travel). Travel grants for under-represented participants.

fwwmeu-brussels-2027.about:
Future We Want Model European Union (FWWMEU) Brussels, 18–20 March 2027, is the EU-simulation edition of the Future We Want programme. It opens with workshops delivered by MEPs, ministers and international experts, then delegates debate in a simulated European Parliament and Council of the EU over three days in the capital of Europe.

High-school delegates (ages 13–19) and university delegates (ages 17–26) from any country can register as individuals or as a delegation; high-school delegations must bring a faculty advisor. No prior MUN experience is required: first-timers are placed in introductory committees and experienced delegates in advanced ones. Country/NGO assignments are released in rounds, background guides are provided, and position papers are due a few weeks before the event.

Registration is first come, first served (early registration is open and regular registration opens 2 November 2026); late registration opens 10 January 2027 and all conference fees are due by 7 February 2027. Financial-aid (scholarship) applications open during the cycle, and invitation letters for visas are issued after payment. It suits students who want a large, international MUN experience abroad focused on EU policy-making.
highlights: International delegates from many countries; individual or delegation registration
Workshops with MEPs, ministers and experts; simulated European Parliament and Council of the EU
Financial-aid applications available during the registration cycle
fwwmeu-brussels-2027.eligibility: High-school students aged 13–19 and university students aged 17–26 who are currently enrolled, from any country. Individuals may register alone; high-school delegations need at least one faculty advisor. English is the working language; no prior MUN experience needed.
how_to_apply: Open the FWWMEU Brussels page and read Registration & Costs and Terms & Conditions
Register as a delegate (or observer) individually or as a delegation
Apply for financial aid during the scholarship window if needed
Pay all conference fees by 7 February 2027 and book the partner hotel package if wanted
Request a visa invitation letter after payment if required
Receive your country/NGO assignment and submit the position paper by 22 February 2027
fwwmeu-brussels-2027.costs: Conference fee per participant (Basic conference-only package or packages with partner-hotel accommodation, prices shown in the FWW registration system); optional Certified Training USD 49. Flights, visas and meals outside the package are extra. Partial financial aid can be requested.

hkbu-physics-summer-research-experience-.about:
The Department of Physics at Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU) runs a Summer Research Experience Programme in which outstanding students spend about one month in July–August working on research with a faculty member. Research groups in the department cover areas such as green energy and smart technology, photonics and metamaterials, condensed-matter and biological physics, and complex systems and neural dynamics; the programme also introduces students to HKBU's MPhil/PhD research degrees.

Applicants email the completed application form with supporting documents and a CV to the department. Details of support are given in the programme document linked from the call.

iceland-international-summer-school-mode.about:
Each year the Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies and the University of Iceland's Faculty of Humanities run the International Summer School in Modern Icelandic Language and Culture. In 2027 it runs from 5 to 29 July. The on-campus programme in Edda, the new house of Icelandic studies in Reykjavík, has 80 hours of instruction (70 hours of grammar, practice and reading, 10 hours of lectures on modern Icelandic society, culture, history, literature and geology), three excursions to historical and geological sites, two day trips to West and South Iceland and museum visits. An online version on Zoom offers 40 hours without excursions.

Classes are in two groups (A1–A2 and A2–B1) set by a free online placement test; instruction is mainly in Icelandic with English as support, in classes of about 10–19. Applicants are expected to complete the free Icelandic Online – Survival course first. The school suits students and adults of any background who want a serious start in Icelandic.

ihbb-azerbaijan-2027.about:

middlebury-language-schools-summer-2027.about:
The Middlebury Language Schools, run by Middlebury College since 1915, offer intensive summer immersion programmes, mostly on the Middlebury campus in Vermont. Students sign the Language Pledge, committing to use only the target language for the whole programme, and live, eat and take part in co-curricular activities together by language; an eight-week programme such as Arabic (18 June – 13 August 2027) carries 12 semester hours of credit, and levels run from beginner to advanced.

Applicants are typically university students, graduates and professionals (adults); international applicants are welcome but need a US visa allowing full-time study, which Middlebury's ISSS supports after enrolment. Funding includes merit fellowships such as Fellows for Peace, Conflict Transformation and Kress fellowships (deadline 15 December 2026) and partial need-based grants (up to US$7,200 for Arabic) awarded first come, first served, so applying by the 15 November priority deadline matters.

ntu-taiwan-spring-plus-chinese-language-.about:
NTU's Spring+ Chinese Language and Culture Program is a compact three-week version of its summer Mandarin course, running from 2 to 24 March 2027 in Taipei. Students take three hours of Chinese a day (three to four comprehensive lessons over the programme), practise with NTU student tutors, and follow the English-taught Exploring Taiwan course on history, festivals, arts, food and indigenous heritage, with site visits and a one-day trip.

It is open to beginners and experienced learners aged 16 or over with intermediate English; native Chinese speakers cannot apply. Successful participants get a certificate and a transcript with 3 NTU short-term credits. Optional discounted housing (USD 600–800) is booked via the portal. Applications are open until 12 January 2027.
highlights: Three weeks of Mandarin at Taiwan's top university
All levels, open from age 16
3 NTU credits; applications close 12 January 2027
ntu-taiwan-spring-plus-chinese-language-.eligibility: Age 16+, any nationality except native Chinese speakers; intermediate English (about TOEIC 600; no score required). One programme per session.

ntu-taiwan-summer-plus-chinese-language-.about:
National Taiwan University, Taiwan's leading university, runs the Summer+ Chinese Language and Culture Program through its NTU Plus Academy. From 21 June to 30 July 2027 students study Chinese for three hours a day (five to seven comprehensive lessons across the six weeks), practise with NTU student tutors at a 'Tutor Station', and take the English-taught Exploring Taiwan course on history and society, art, music and food culture, with site visits, indigenous-heritage field trips and a one-day trip. Successful participants receive a certificate and a transcript with 7 NTU short-term credits (5 Chinese, 2 Exploring Taiwan).

The programme is open to complete beginners and experienced learners aged 16 or over (so strong high-school students can join); applicants need intermediate English (around TOEIC 600) for the culture course, and native Chinese speakers cannot apply. Optional discounted off-campus housing (USD 1,050–1,350) is booked through the application portal, and the programme fee includes tuition, orientation, cultural courses, activities and accident insurance.

Open to all levels and to applicants aged 16+
NTU student tutors and cultural field trips

polyu-international-summer-school-2027.about:
PolyU's International Summer School brings students from around the world to its Hung Hom campus each July. Each participant takes one 3-credit subject (39 contact hours, taught in English, with attendance, assessments and a final exam) chosen from a list across PolyU's faculties, and joins enrichment activities, local tours, a research-education talk with faculty, a buddy programme with PolyU students and a closing party. In 2026 the programme ran from orientation on 6 July to closing on 30 July, with halls open 3 July – 7 August; a free transcript is issued for credit transfer.

Non-local fee-paying students must have completed the first year of their university studies by the start, be in good academic standing and show English at TOEFL iBT 80 / IELTS 6.0 or equivalent (waivers for some qualifications). Students at PolyU exchange partner universities are nominated by their home university and have the programme and housing fees waived.

rotary-perugia-international-youth-cours.about:
Every July the Rotary Club of Perugia runs its International Rotary Youth Course (the 69th edition was 6–31 July 2026) in collaboration with the University for Foreigners of Perugia, Italy's oldest school of Italian for foreigners. The eight scholarship holders attend the university's Italian language and culture courses for the month and join activities organised by the club, such as visits to other cities and Rotary events, with the aim of fostering understanding between peoples.

The scholarship covers course enrolment, accommodation for the whole course and meals; students pay only travel, compulsory health insurance and personal expenses. Candidates must be 18–25, enrolled at a university, live abroad and hold a valid passport. Selection is made by the Rotary Club on the basis of the CV, and applications are emailed to the club using the official form (in Italian).

One month of Italian language and culture in Perugia
Open to university students aged 18–25 of any nationality living abroad

rotary-perugia-international-youth-cours.costs: Covered: Italian course fees, accommodation and meals for the whole course, Rotary activities. Not covered: travel, compulsory health insurance and personal expenses.

tau-summer-research-program-sciences-202.about:
Tel Aviv University, with about 400 labs and 125 research institutes, runs an eight-week Summer Research Program in the Sciences led by Prof. Ben Maoz. Participants join a participating lab as full members of the research team, carry out an independent research project under experienced scientists and present their findings at a final symposium to the group and faculty. In 2026 it ran from 3 June to 30 July; no formal TAU academic credit is awarded.

The programme is aimed at science students who want hands-on research experience abroad and help choosing a future research track. The Student Life team adds cultural and social activities, and short-term students can apply for TAU housing.

Final symposium presenting your own results

tau-winter-hebrew-ulpan-2027.about:
Tel Aviv University's Hebrew Language Studies Unit runs short intensive Hebrew Ulpan courses in summer and winter. The Winter Ulpan runs from 21 January to 18 February 2027 on the Ramat Aviv campus, with classes Sunday to Thursday from 8:30 to 13:00, focused purely on Hebrew and covering speaking, listening, reading and writing for everyday, academic and professional use.

Courses may be offered from complete beginner to advanced, depending on enrolment, and are open to international students, professionals and anyone wanting to learn Hebrew in Israel. Participants can apply for TAU housing for short-term programmes, subject to availability.

Option of TAU student housing

uantwerp-almeria-winter-school-resources.about:
Organised by the University of Antwerp with the University of Almería's Center for the Study of Migrations and Intercultural Relations (CEMyRI) and the Atlas Center for Bioethics, this winter school runs from 7 to 13 February 2027 on the University of Almería campus in southern Spain. Using Almería's intensive greenhouse horticulture as a case, it explores the history of water management, labour migration and the shift to renewable energy, through in-class seminars on relational ethics and the social embeddedness of markets, bus excursions, a visit to the Alcazaba and conversations with people who live and work in the region.

The school is designed for master's students, PhD students and professionals interested in environmental or health humanities, environmental politics, social justice or bioethics; applicants need at least two completed years of higher education in a relevant field. Successful completion of all assessment tasks earns 3–6 ECTS credits and a micro-credential.
highlights: Field-based learning in Almería's greenhouse region
Relational ethics, water, energy and migration in one case
Low EUR 300 fee, 3–6 ECTS credits
uantwerp-almeria-winter-school-resources.eligibility: Master's and PhD students and professionals in relevant fields, with at least two completed years of higher education; good English. All nationalities; non-EU citizens may need a Schengen visa (Georgian citizens are visa-free for short stays).

Wait for the selection outcome
Pay the fee and book travel and housing in Almería

Travel, housing and other meals not included (campus lunch menus about EUR 6).

uantwerp-summer-school-childrens-literat.about:
The University of Antwerp's Children's Literature Summer School (28 June – 2 July 2027) is devoted to the theme 'Body and Mind', approached from several disciplinary perspectives. Students attend lectures by specialists in children's and young adult literature, take part in interactive workshops and two excursions, and learn alongside an international group whose diversity is treated as part of the course.

It mainly targets master's and PhD students, but senior researchers and professionals interested in children's literature studies are also welcome; participants must have completed at least three full years of undergraduate study. PhD students can present their projects or give a 20-minute paper in two dedicated workshops. Applying by 1 February 2027 secures the early-bird fee.

uantwerp-summer-school-film-history-2027.about:
The University of Antwerp's Film History summer school (4–10 July 2027) takes place at De Studio – De Cinema in Antwerp. Each edition is built around two themes: in 2027 the first is 'Hollywood's Other Stars: Difference and the Business of Stardom in Classical Hollywood Cinema', with a second strand still to be announced. Around twenty rare archival films are screened in proper cinema conditions, combined with expert lectures, in-depth seminars and discussion with scholars, critics and students from around the world.

The school is designed for master's and PhD students in film and media studies or related disciplines, and for film professionals with a strong interest in film history; participants need bachelor-level knowledge of film history and theory.

uantwerp-summer-school-responsible-fashi.about:
This University of Antwerp summer school combines Antwerp's pioneering independent fashion ecosystem with Parisian luxury heritage. The Antwerp week (28 June – 2 July 2027) and the Paris sessions (5–7 July 2027) look at how fashion businesses respond to environmental, social and economic challenges through sustainability, entrepreneurship and responsible management, with workshops, group discussions and real-world cases from industry.

It is designed for fashion professionals, entrepreneurs and third-year bachelor's, master's and PhD students who want to drive positive change in the industry, and values the exchange between academia and practice. Participants arrange and pay for their own accommodation and travel, including the trip from Antwerp to Paris.

Open to 3rd-year bachelor's students upwards and professionals

uoft-create-engineering-design-challenge.about:
CREATE: Engineering Design Challenges is a summer programme run by U of T Engineering's outreach office on the St. George campus in downtown Toronto. Each week-long course is built around a design challenge inspired by one of the Faculty's engineering disciplines: students work through the engineering design cycle with practical activities, laboratory experiments and site visits, guided by current U of T undergraduate and graduate students. It complements the more lecture-based DEEP programme (the two share one application).

In 2027 CREATE runs in six one-week sessions between 5 July and 20 August (Monday–Friday). Admitted students can register for up to six courses; an on-campus residence option is available. There are separate tracks for grades 9/10 and 11/12, and international students pay a higher weekly fee.

world-scholars-cup-amman-round-2027.about:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students that rewards curiosity rather than memorisation. Teams of three study an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music, literature and social studies, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz). Rounds also include community events such as the Scholar's Show (talent show).

This is a regional round in Amman, Jordan, on 23–24 April 2027, hosted by International Community School Amman. Students can join through a school club or as an independent team of three from any country; results can qualify teams for a Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.
